# Configuration

Every setting is an environment variable. `config.FromEnv` is the only
place that reads them, and it refuses on start what cannot work: two backup
targets, a bucket with no region or no credentials, an interval under a minute, a
prefix that would need escaping in a signed URL.

The defaults below are what the process uses when the variable is unset. To see
what one process actually read, ask it:

```bash
byge doctor
```

Where the server listens. `LISTEN_ADDR` is a whole address, so it is also how you bind one interface instead of every one of them.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `LISTEN_ADDR` | *(unset)* | wins over `SERVER_PORT` when set |
| `SERVER_PORT` | `17808` | the port, unless `LISTEN_ADDR` names one |

Which store holds the boards and how to reach it. The `DB_*` variables build a Postgres connection string and are read for that backend only; `STORAGE=memory` keeps the boards in the process and loses them on exit.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `STORAGE` | `postgres` | postgres \| sqlite \| memory |
| `DATABASE_URL` | *(unset)* | a full DSN; wins over every `DB_*` variable; a secret: reports keep the address and take out the password |
| `DB_USER` | `user` |  |
| `DB_PASS` | `password` | a secret: reports say `[set]` and never the value |
| `DB_HOST` | `postgres` |  |
| `DB_PORT` | `5432` |  |
| `DB_NAME` | `kanban` |  |
| `DB_SSLMODE` | `disable` | disable, require, verify-full, as libpq spells them |
| `SQLITE_PATH` | `/data/kanban.db` | `STORAGE=sqlite` only; the image has a volume at /data |

Who is making the request. See [docs/adr/0005](adr/0005-request-identity.md) for why proxy and access are not interchangeable, and why none is a defensible default.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_MODE` | `none` | none takes every request as anonymous |
| `AUTH_HEADER` | `X-Forwarded-Email` | the header read in proxy mode |
| `ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN` | *(unset)* | e.g. team.cloudflareaccess.com |
| `ACCESS_AUD` | *(unset)* | the Access application's AUD tag |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | `false` | true: a request with no identity is refused rather than served |
| `AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_OWNER` | *(unset)* | an address: the only caller who may claim a board that has no owner, and who sees an ownerless board meanwhile; lowercased on read |

Where the caller's groups come from, so that a board can be granted a role on a group the identity provider keeps rather than one kept here. Both are empty by default: a deployment that sets neither has only the groups in its own database, which is the setup that needs nothing configured anywhere else. `AUTH_GROUPS_HEADER` is read in proxy mode and holds one comma-separated list. It is worth only as much as the proxy in front of the port: a caller that reaches the port another way sets its own. That was already true of `AUTH_HEADER`, but an address decided whose name went on a card and a group decides who may write.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_GROUPS_HEADER` | *(unset)* | proxy mode only, one comma-separated list; trusted only as far as the proxy in front of the port |

`ACCESS_GROUPS_CLAIM` is the claim read in access mode. Inside a signed assertion, so a caller cannot choose its own.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `ACCESS_GROUPS_CLAIM` | *(unset)* | access mode only; empty means the claim named groups, where Cloudflare puts them unless the connection maps them elsewhere |

A service identity for a trusted in-cluster caller that cannot carry a Cloudflare assertion, read in access mode. See [docs/adr/0005](adr/0005-request-identity.md) for the trust basis: a header is a claim by whatever wrote it, and is sound only where the port is unreachable except through the thing that sets it. The network policy in front of this port already guarantees that, which is the same basis proxy mode documents for its own header. Both empty by default: a deployment that sets neither has no service identity and the branch is inert, exactly like AUTH_BOOTSTRAP_OWNER.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_SERVICE_HEADER` | *(unset)* | access mode only; the header whose mere presence marks a request as the service caller, set only by a network-isolated in-cluster caller |
| `AUTH_SERVICE_GROUP` | *(unset)* | the idp group name that caller is treated as holding, so the owner can grant it through the access page; lowercased on read |

Who the board says may see it, as a mail address list: `Ada Lovelace <ada@example.com>, grace@example.com`. Shown in the app bar and nowhere else. This is a copy of a list kept somewhere else, so one address per person is what reads well, and the sign-in in front of the board is what the copy has to agree with. It is drawn only for a caller the board identified. In `access` mode that means a verified assertion; in `proxy` mode it means a header, which anything that can reach the port can set, so a port reachable any other way wants `AUTH_REQUIRED` as well.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_VIEWERS` | *(unset)* | displayed, never enforced: the board admits whoever the sign-in admits |

Who has a picture instead of initials, as address=github-login pairs. Unset means initials and no outbound request; [docs/adr/0008](adr/0008-avatars-are-proxied.md) has why the server fetches the picture rather than the browser.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AVATARS` | *(unset)* | a pair that is not a pair is refused on start, not skipped |

Where the scheduler puts snapshots and how often. Neither a directory nor a bucket means no schedule, and `byge export` is then the only way a snapshot gets taken.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `BACKUP_INTERVAL` | `24h` | 0 turns the schedule off; under a minute is refused |
| `BACKUP_KEEP` | `7` | 0 keeps every snapshot; the rest go after a successful write |
| `BACKUP_DIR` | *(unset)* | a directory on a volume that outlives the container |
| `BACKUP_S3_BUCKET` | *(unset)* | the other target; set one of the two, not both |
| `BACKUP_S3_PREFIX` | *(unset)* | normalised to end in /, so one bucket can hold several boards |
| `BACKUP_S3_REGION` | *(unset)* | or `AWS_REGION`; required with a bucket, it is part of the signature |
| `BACKUP_S3_ENDPOINT` | *(unset)* | empty for AWS; anything else is addressed path-style; a secret: reports keep the address and take out the password |

The usual AWS names, so a deployment that already injects credentials for something else does not need a second set under our own names.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` | *(unset)* | required with a bucket: there is no credential chain |
| `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | *(unset)* | required with a bucket; a secret: reports say `[set]` and never the value |
| `AWS_SESSION_TOKEN` | *(unset)* | only for temporary credentials; a secret: reports say `[set]` and never the value |

What the process does on start, and how much it says while it runs.

| Variable | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTO_MIGRATE` | `true` | false: run `byge migrate` yourself |
| `LOG_LEVEL` | `info` | debug \| info \| warn \| error |
| `LOG_FORMAT` | `text` | text \| json |
